C0.quote: all deterministic voting rules have unbounded distortion
C0.note: Distortion of voting rules (welfare performance of rankings-based rules) under a behavioural model of voters.

C1.quote: we show that public-spirited voting can substantially reduce the distortion of several voting rules
C1.note: Most results are distortion bounds (WD). Sec. 4.3 uses Muller-Satterthwaite to prove an impossibility (AX).

C2.1.quote: A preference profile 𝝅 is the 𝑛-tuple of all 𝑛 voters' rankings

C2.2.quote: Voter 𝑖 expresses their preferences over alternatives as a strict, complete ranking 𝜋𝑖

C2.3.quote: We define a utility matrix 𝑈 ∈ [0, 1] 𝑛×𝑚
C2.3.note: Utilities and public-spirit levels are held attitudes.

C2.4.quote: 𝑣𝑖 (𝑎, 𝜸, 𝑈 ) > 𝑣𝑖 (𝑏, 𝜸, 𝑈 ) =⇒ 𝑎 ≻𝜋𝑖 𝑏
C2.4.note: Rankings (input) and utilities/PS-values (held) have separate notation, linked by a behavioural model. The input is not equal to utilities but derived from PS-values.

C3.1.quote: The possibility of some voters being strategic opens several questions
C3.1.note: Voters rank by PS-values; strategic manipulation is left to future work. Misreports in Sec. 5.2 are behavioural errors, not strategic.

C3.2.quote: voter 𝑖 ranks alternatives in order of their PS-value
C3.2.note: The paper states in words that voters rank according to their PS-values.

C3.3.note: The behavioural model is motivated by social-science observations of public spirit, but no incentive/SP/empirical reason is given for ranking by PS-value without strategising.

C4.1.quote: alternatives are ordered in decreasing order of PS-value
C4.1.note: Ranking is defined as induced by PS-values, which are a convex combination of utility and average welfare.

C5.1.quote: the ratio between the respective welfares of the highest-welfare alternative

C5.2.quote: sw(𝑎, 𝑈 ) denote the utilitarian social welfare
C5.2.note: Distortion evaluated against held cardinal utilities U, defined separately from rankings.

VOT.quote_behav: voter 𝑖 ranks alternatives in order of their PS-value
VOT.note: Voters follow a fixed behavioural rule (PS-value ranking). In Sec. 5.2 they know utilities and welfares with errors, but behaviour is not strategic.

DES.note: The designer is mentioned only informally (footnote 3).

C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

claims.quote: our results suggest an implementable approach to improving the welfare outcomes of elections
interventions that promote public spirited voting can only help
This evidence suggests that public-spirited voting behavior can be cultivated

C9.1.note: Claims about real institutions (deliberation) and voters' welfare.

C9.2.quote: Of course, these results arise from a theoretical model
C9.2.note: Needed: deliberation actually raises γ (cited, partially empirical); voters non-strategic (acknowledged as future work, so mostly stated); and the claim 'can only help' needs monotonicity, which fails instance-wise (Thm 4.11), partly acknowledged. The assumption that deliberation yields accurate welfare estimates is stated only as theorised. Marked SOME-UNSTATED with some doubt.
